emotionalArc: Awe and curiosity → dread and entrapment → surprise and defiance → sorrow and recognition → grief and rupture → hard-won awe at the legacy cost

transition.description: Cold open: handwritten title card slaps onto yellow notebook paper — stark ink, no fanfare.

narrativeIntent.narrativeRole: Snap the viewer into the central paradox before they can look away.
narrativeIntent.keyMessage: A 19-year-old with zero armor walked into a thousand-year machine — and won.

scenes.script: She was 19. Zero media training. About to walk into a thousand-year-old machine.

transition.description: New notebook page slides in from the right — a family tree sketched in ink appears.

narrativeIntent.narrativeRole: Establish the historical irony that reframes everything that follows.
narrativeIntent.keyMessage: Diana was more deeply English aristocratic than the German-born Windsors she was marrying into.
narrativeIntent.persuasion: Dramatic irony — the audience knows what the palace missed

scenes.script: The Windsors only changed their German surname in 1917. The Spencers were Tudor aristocracy for five centuries.

transition.description: Page blurs and re-settles — lighter, more personal handwriting emerges, as if a diary entry.

narrativeIntent.narrativeRole: Show the human wreckage the palace completely failed to see.
narrativeIntent.keyMessage: Diana entered the marriage already broken — unwanted at birth, abandoned by her mother, boiling with unresolved rage.
narrativeIntent.persuasion: Specificity — concrete details that make abstraction visceral

scenes.script: Her parents wanted a boy. She was left unnamed for a week. Her mother's footsteps on gravel were her earliest memory of loss.

transition.description: Ink-stamped corporate logo graphic — hard block letters read THE FIRM — then dissolves into architectural floor plan.

narrativeIntent.narrativeRole: Name the true antagonist: not Charles, but the institution itself.
narrativeIntent.keyMessage: The monarchy isn't a family — it's a billion-dollar corporation whose primary product is emotional concealment.
narrativeIntent.persuasion: Reframing — replace familiar narrative with accurate structural lens

scenes.script: The monarchy isn't a family. It's a corporation — wealth preservation, image control, zero tolerance for emotional visibility.

transition.description: Camera zooms into a single ink-drawn figure dwarfed by towering institutional columns — scale communicates the horror.

narrativeIntent.narrativeRole: Show the collision point — how the firm absorbed Diana and what it did to her.
narrativeIntent.keyMessage: The palace viewed her despair as an operational glitch, not a cry for help.
narrativeIntent.persuasion: Contrast — corporate language applied to human suffering

scenes.script: Her bulimia, self-harm, depression — the firm called them glitches. Embarrassments to be managed. The brand had to be protected.

transition.description: Dissolve into a scene sketch of a hand extended — simple ink gesture, no glove, enormous negative space around it.

narrativeIntent.narrativeRole: The pivot: show the moment she found her weapon — physical touch as political act.
narrativeIntent.keyMessage: One ungloved handshake with an AIDS patient did more than a decade of government pamphlets.
narrativeIntent.persuasion: Concrete example as proof of mechanism

scenes.script: 1987. AIDS ward. She shook a dying man's hand — no gloves. A silent visual that shattered a global panic.

transition.sharedMotif: open hand becoming a bridge toward the viewer
transition.description: The extended hand from scene 6 morphs into a crowd reaching back — same gesture, global scale.

narrativeIntent.narrativeRole: Name the mechanism: she created a rival royal court built on public empathy instead of hereditary power.
narrativeIntent.keyMessage: She generated consent the Crown couldn't manufacture — by being physically present with the suffering.
narrativeIntent.persuasion: Theory of the equal — power flows upward through touch, not down through distance

scenes.script: Where the Queen offered distance, Diana offered touch. She walked into minefields, sat on amputees' beds, refused to wear hats so she could properly hug children.

transition.description: Hard cut — bold ink silhouette of a figure in a cocktail dress, tabloid-headline text strips frame it.

narrativeIntent.narrativeRole: Show her second weapon: fashion as wordless political warfare.
narrativeIntent.keyMessage: The night Charles confessed adultery on TV, Diana walked out in a dress she'd kept waiting three years — and buried his story.
narrativeIntent.persuasion: Premeditation as proof of strategic mastery

scenes.script: June 1994. Charles admitted the affair on national TV. Diana stepped out in the revenge dress and erased him from the front pages — without saying a word.

transition.description: Classified-file folder slides open — cassette tape sketched inside, handwritten labels, spy-novel texture.

narrativeIntent.narrativeRole: Prove she was a brilliant combatant — not just a victim — by detailing her espionage tactics.
narrativeIntent.keyMessage: She dictated her own devastating exposé onto cassette tapes and smuggled them out in a doctor's bicycle basket.
narrativeIntent.persuasion: Narrative detail — the logistics prove the intent

scenes.script: She couldn't meet the author directly. So she recorded everything onto tapes — smuggled out of Kensington Palace in a bicycle basket.

transition.description: Ink splashes outward — same face rendered in fragments across different perspectives, Rorschach-like ink blot structure.

narrativeIntent.narrativeRole: State the central thesis: she stopped being a person and became a mirror for how people feel about power.
narrativeIntent.keyMessage: The establishment saw a threat to order. Marginalized communities saw their own experience in an institution that demands everything and protects nothing.
narrativeIntent.persuasion: Dual-audience contrast — same facts, opposite readings reveal the deeper truth

scenes.script: At a certain point she stopped being a person. She became a canvas — and everyone projected their own relationship with power onto her.

transition.description: Stark cut to a single bare pole drawn in ink against white — minimal, charged, pointed silence.

narrativeIntent.narrativeRole: Show the rupture: her death forced the Crown to publicly perform the emotion she'd spent fifteen years demanding.
narrativeIntent.keyMessage: A bare flagpole broke a thousand-year institution — the monarchy had to learn to feel in public, or lose the consent of the people.
narrativeIntent.persuasion: Object as argument — the flagpole becomes proof of her posthumous power

scenes.script: She died. The palace went silent. The public saw a bare flagpole and called it cruelty. The Queen broke centuries of protocol and came home to grieve in public.

transition.description: Zoom out to reveal the full notebook — all previous sketches visible as one interconnected map, then final ink title closes it.

narrativeIntent.narrativeRole: Land the lasting provocation: her playbook is still running, and the question of whether the firm can survive it is still open.
narrativeIntent.keyMessage: Every royal demanding privacy, every celebrity bypassing media gatekeepers with a raw documentary — that's her blueprint.
narrativeIntent.persuasion: Living legacy — make the historical immediately present

scenes.script: Next time you see a royal go rogue or a celebrity bare their soul in a documentary — you're watching her playbook. Written in blood. Still running.
